question.problem:
Let $Q$ be an orthogonal linear transformation. Which of the following are orthogonal sets?

I. $U=\{Q([\begin{aligned}4 \\ 3\end{aligned}]),Q([\begin{aligned}5 \\ -1\end{aligned}])\}$

II. $V=\{Q([\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 3\end{aligned}]),Q([\begin{aligned}3 \\ -2 \\ \frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}]),Q([\begin{aligned}2 \\ 4 \\ 6\end{aligned}])\}$

III. $W=\{Q([\begin{aligned}5 \\ -3\end{aligned}]),Q([\begin{aligned}-3 \\ -5\end{aligned}])\}$
question.worked_solution:
Since $Q$ is orthogonal, we have that $Q(x)\cdot Q(y)=x\cdot y$ for any vectors $x$ and $y.$

Let's denote the elements of $U,W,$ and $V$ respectively as 

$\,$ $\{Q({u}_{1}),Q({u}_{2})\},\,$ $\{Q({v}_{1}),Q({v}_{2}),Q({v}_{3})\},\,$ and $\,\{Q({w}_{1}),Q({w}_{2})\}.$

The sets $U,V,$ and $W$ are orthogonal if the following conditions on each set hold:

- $Q({u}_{1})\cdot Q({u}_{2})=0.$

- $Q({v}_{1})\cdot Q({v}_{2})=0,\,Q({v}_{1})\cdot Q({v}_{3})=0,\,Q({v}_{2})\cdot Q({v}_{3})=0.$

- $Q({w}_{1})\cdot Q({w}_{2})=0.$

With that in mind, let's examine our sets in turn.

- For the set $U,$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}Q({u}_{1})\cdot Q({u}_{2}) & ={u}_{1}\cdot {u}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 3\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}5 \\ -1\end{aligned}]=20-3=17\ne 0.\,\times \end{aligned}
$$

So, $U$ is not and orthogonal set.

- For the Set $V,$ notice that 

$$
\begin{aligned}Q({v}_{1})\cdot Q({v}_{2}) & ={v}_{1}\cdot {v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 3\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}3 \\ -2 \\ \frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}]=3-4+1=0,\,✓ \\ Q({v}_{1})\cdot Q({v}_{3}) & ={v}_{1}\cdot {v}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 3\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}2 \\ 4 \\ 6\end{aligned}]=2+8+18=28\ne 0.\,\times \end{aligned}
$$

So, $V$ is not an orthogonal set.

- For the set $W,$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}Q({w}_{1})\cdot Q({w}_{2}) & ={w}_{1}\cdot {w}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -3\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}-3 \\ -5\end{aligned}]=-15+15=0.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

So, the set $W$ is orthogonal.

Therefore, the correct answer is "$W$ only".
